beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Permission Paradox examines ideas evaluated through categories built from the past.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks how institutions can test unfamiliar possibilities without rewarding persuasive speculation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AI sharpens the problem when candidate novelty outpaces society's capacity to evaluate it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book proposes conditional review, bounded inquiry, and funding arrangements that purchase learning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a way to inspect this tension without dividing people into visionaries and fools.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine an inventor proposing a leak sensor whose performance has not yet been tested.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An evaluator usually reasons forward from existing evidence, precedent, and recognized categories.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Both approaches can be reasonable while producing a persistent mismatch.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also recognizes that an unfamiliar idea may simply be wrong.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its question is how to distinguish responsible testing from either premature rejection or technological credulity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Longview is the book's proposed approach to conditional assessment of future potential.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A small, controlled test could show whether that sensor detects the leak.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reversibility, meaningful benefit, protected participants, and learning value remain important conditions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The funding discussion connects short experimental cycles with patience for difficult research.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These are institutional proposals to investigate, not automatic reasons to approve every unconventional claim.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the mismatch between candidate novelty and the capacity to evaluate it.
